BlenderWorld

Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References

Website · Quickstart · Evaluation · Documentation

📑 Technical Report  |  🤗 Hugging Face  |  🤖 ModelScope

[![Overview of BlenderWorld: references on the left and top lead to editable 3D scenes on the right and bottom](docs/assets/benchmark-overview.jpg)](docs/assets/benchmark-overview.jpg) *From real-world references to editable 3D scenes. The benchmark contains 223 tasks across 9 categories and 22 subcategories; references appear on the left/top and GPT-6-Astra outputs on the right/bottom.* BlenderWorld evaluates agents on realistic 3D creation requests in Blender. Agents receive a task brief, reference media when applicable, and any declared specification files, then deliver an editable Blender project and the requested exports. Run your model with any generation harness, collect one submission ZIP per task, and evaluate it with `bw evaluate`. [Harbor integration](docs/harbor.md) is available as an optional generation and verification adapter. ## Dataset BlenderWorld contains **223 tasks and 2,651 binary criteria**, spanning products, architecture, environments, characters, animation, and scientific visualization. All tasks use neutral IDs from `bw_0001` to `bw_0223`. | Input | Tasks | | --- | ---: | | Text | 78 | | Image + text | 130 | | Video + text | 15 | | Total | 223 | **59 tasks** also include specification attachments with requirements on dimensions, materials, or camera settings. These files can accompany visual references. [![Dataset statistics showing application scenarios, reference and specification types, and category importance](docs/assets/dataset-statistics.png)](docs/assets/dataset-statistics.png) *Dataset statistics. (a) shows the 11 largest application scenarios, covering 213 of 223 tasks; (b) reference and specification types may co-occur; (c) the inner ring shows category and the outer ring shows importance.*
How the benchmark is built
[![Benchmark construction flow from production briefs through validation and rubric review](docs/assets/benchmark-construction.png)](docs/assets/benchmark-construction.png) *From production briefs to verifiable requirements. Diverse tasks and references undergo structural and semantic validation, followed by independent rubric review.*
## Quickstart ### 1. Install and download Use Python 3.10+ on Linux. Download the dataset and check every task and resource: ```bash git clone https://github.com/QwenLM/BlenderWorld.git cd BlenderWorld python -m pip install -e . bw download --output data/BlenderWorld bw verify data/BlenderWorld bw list data/BlenderWorld --modality image ``` To use an existing local dataset, pass its directory to `--dataset`. To pin a published revision, pass its commit SHA to `bw download --revision`. ### 2. Prepare, generate, and package Prepare the inputs for one generation agent: ```bash bw prepare --dataset data/BlenderWorld --task-id bw_0001 --output work/bw_0001 ``` The prepared workspace contains `query.txt`, `input.json`, reference media, and declared attachments. Give the agent access to this workspace and Blender through its normal coding or MCP tools. Save the primary project as `model-output/final.blend`, alongside its requested exports and texture dependencies. Keep inputs and evaluation rubrics outside this output directory. Package its contents as one ZIP for the task: ```bash bw pack-submission --source model-output --task-id bw_0001 \ --output submissions/bw_0001.zip ``` The ZIP contains `final.blend` at its root, with optional `textures/` and `outputs/` folders. Ordinary ZIP tools are supported too. See [the complete public submission format](docs/submissions.md). Generate projects with **Blender 4.2.10**. When using the bundled coding-agent environment, the other pins are **Node.js 22.17.0, Codex CLI 0.147.0, and Claude Code 2.1.220**. ### 3. Evaluate Evaluation needs Blender 4.2.10, Node.js 22.17.0, ffmpeg/ffprobe, and the configured Claude Code 2.1.220 CLI for rendering and scene inspection, plus a vision-capable Chat Completions endpoint. Configure the endpoint and key variables described in [the evaluation guide](docs/evaluation.md) in your shell. Model aliases must exist at their configured endpoints; the paper uses GPT-5.6-terra for all three evaluator roles. ```bash bw evaluate --dataset data/BlenderWorld --submissions submissions \ --task-id bw_0001 --output runs/one-task --dry-run bw evaluate --dataset data/BlenderWorld --submissions submissions \ --task-id bw_0001 --output runs/one-task --resume ``` Omit `--task-id` for all 223 tasks. Missing or failed submissions receive zero and remain in the selected denominator. `--dry-run` writes a plan without invoking Blender or model services. JSON and CSV results are written to the run directory. ## Evaluation [![Evaluation pipeline combining adaptive renders, scene inspection, rubric scoring, and visual-quality ratings](docs/assets/evaluation-pipeline.png)](docs/assets/evaluation-pipeline.png) *The paper pipeline combines 8 adaptive views and scene inspection with a weighted binary rubric and 8 visual-quality ratings, weighted 50:50. The figure shows the paper setup (Cycles, GPU, and Blender MCP); the public evaluator also supports CPU Cycles and accepts submissions from any generation harness.* The renderer selects **eight adaptive views**, using Cycles at **1024 × 1024 and 64 samples**. It preserves the submitted scene and allows up to **two corrective re-renders per view**. Original authored images and sampled animation frames provide additional evidence. Scene-inspection criteria are assigned to Agent-as-Judge; visual criteria and eight holistic quality dimensions are assigned to the VLM. Each binary criterion has importance weight 1, 2, or 3. ```text Rubric score = 100 × Σ(weight × pass) / Σ(weight) Dimension score = 10 × mean(eight ratings from 1 to 10) Final score = 0.5 × rubric score + 0.5 × dimension score ``` The public protocol applies no score cap. It requires fresh evaluator renders, complete structural verdicts, and all eight dimension ratings. See [the protocol and runtime guide](docs/evaluation.md) for configuration, evidence, and resuming runs. ## Documentation Read the [dataset format](docs/dataset.md) for task records and resources, the [submission ZIP format](docs/submissions.md) before packaging results, and the [evaluation protocol](docs/evaluation.md) for runtime configuration, evidence, and resuming runs. [Harbor integration](docs/harbor.md) describes the optional generation and verification adapter.

# BlenderWorld
BlenderWorld is the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, a unified evaluation protocol is established: The submitted Blender projects are rendered from multiple viewpoints and evaluated against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. For more details, please refer to our Project: [BlenderWorld](https://github.com/QwenLM/BlenderWorld).

# BlenderWorld-Harbor

The benchmark comprises 223 tasks and 2,651 rubric criteria. Each instance includes a Base64-encoded image preview and corresponding JSON data.

The package contains 78 text, 130 image-and-text, and 15 video-and-text tasks.
Use **Harbor 0.23.0**, Python 3.12+ and a GPU-capable Linux sandbox.
The commands below use the Modal backend. [中文使用说明](使用说明.md)

## Task categories

The 223 tasks span **9 categories and 22 subcategories**. Use [taxonomy.csv](taxonomy.csv)
for the per-task mapping, [taxonomy.json](taxonomy.json) for the hierarchy, counts and
figure labels, or [classification_summary.md](classification_summary.md) for a readable table.
Each task also includes `category`, `subcategory`, `category_short`, `subcategory_short`
and `taxonomy_version` in `task.toml` metadata and its evaluator dataset record.

## View tasks and embedded images

Extract the ZIP and open `index.html` in a browser. Search by task ID or query,
or filter by modality. Each task's `environment/inputs/instruction.html` displays
its query, Base64-embedded reference images and declared attachments.
Videos play from the bundled files using relative paths.

All 130 input images are available in `environment/inputs/reference_images.base64.json`.
Each image record includes `path`, `media_type`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `width`, `height`
and a complete `data_uri`. Tasks without input images have an empty `images` array.
The one verifier-only image is in `bw_0182/tests/rubric_reference_images.base64.json`.

```python
import base64, hashlib, json

with open("bw_0006/environment/inputs/reference_images.base64.json") as f:
    image = json.load(f)["images"][0]
raw = base64.b64decode(image["data_uri"].split(",", 1)[1], validate=True)
assert hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == image["sha256"]
```

Base64 decoding returns the full image file bytes. `base64_manifest.json` lists all
image locations and fingerprints. Standard image files are also available for
Harbor agents and the evaluator. The agent's `instruction.md` contains a short text
prompt and file paths; encoded image payloads are in the HTML/JSON files.

## Run with Harbor

```bash
python -m pip install "harbor[modal]==0.23.0"
cd BlenderWorld-harbor-base64
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

Configure Modal credentials with `modal token new`, or use your existing Modal
credentials. You can select another GPU-capable Harbor backend with `--env`.
Harbor 0.23.0's built-in Docker backend does not allocate GPUs from `task.toml`;
use a backend that supports the declared GPU requirement.

Configure the generation agent's provider credentials. For the verifier, set the
environment variables documented in `verifier.env.example`:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `BW_AGENT_JUDGE_ENDPOINT` | Anthropic-compatible endpoint for rendering/scene-inspection agents |
| `BW_AGENT_JUDGE_API_KEY` | Key for that endpoint |
| `BW_VISION_JUDGE_ENDPOINT` | Full Chat Completions endpoint for the vision judge |
| `BW_VISION_JUDGE_API_KEY` | Key for the vision endpoint |
| `BW_RENDER_MODEL` | Optional rendering-agent model alias |
